questions.question: Sami receives a patient who wants veneers on all 8 anterior teeth. He says: 'We prepare all teeth at the same time!' Mina responds: 'Not so fast!' What is the first essential step before preparing veneers?
options: Create a wax-up and a mock-up to validate the aesthetic project
Take radiographs of the teeth involved
Order the veneers from the laboratory immediately
Do a preliminary whitening on all teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The wax-up and mock-up allow the patient to visualize the final result before any irreversible preparation.' Sami: 'I'll do a mock-up first.'

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a smile, says: 'The smile line is very high.' Sami asks: 'Is that a problem?' Why can a high smile line be problematic?
options: It can expose too much gum and compromise aesthetics
It is always more aesthetic than a low line
It allows more teeth to be seen, which is perfect
It facilitates the placement of veneers on molars
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A high smile line shows a lot of gum. This may require prior periodontal treatment.' Sami: 'I'll evaluate the gingival show.'

questions.question: Sami, preparing a veneer, says: 'I prepare 0.5 mm everywhere.' Mina responds: 'Not that simple!' Why is a differentiated preparation needed?
options: The thickness must vary by zone: cervical, incisal, and proximal
The entire preparation must be perfectly uniform
You must prepare deeper on molars
The preparation depends only on the color of the teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Cervical zones are thinner, incisal zones require more thickness.' Sami: 'I'll adapt the preparation according to the zone.'

questions.question: Mina, choosing the shade of veneers, says: 'We must consider translucency.' Sami asks: 'What is translucency?'
options: The ability of ceramic to allow light to pass through
The white color of the ceramic
The resistance of ceramic to impact
The shine of the veneer surface
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Translucency gives a natural appearance by imitating enamel.' Sami: 'I'll choose a ceramic with the right translucency.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a veneer that debonds, says: 'It's the laboratory's fault!' Mina responds: 'Not necessarily.' What are the causes of adhesion failure?
options: Contamination, poor preparation, or incorrect adhesive protocol
Only the quality of the ceramic
Only the patient's fault
Only the type of cement used
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Adhesion is a sensitive process. Contamination or a poor protocol can compromise retention.' Sami: 'I'll check my adhesion protocol.'

questions.question: Mina, seeing an asymmetrical smile, says: 'You need orthodontic treatment first.' Sami asks: 'Why not veneers directly?'
options: Veneers do not correct skeletal or orthodontic asymmetries
Veneers can correct all asymmetries
Orthodontics is faster than veneers
Veneers are cheaper than orthodontics
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Veneers mask but do not correct major asymmetries. Orthodontics is the first step.' Sami: 'I'll do orthodontics first.'

questions.question: Sami, receiving veneers from the laboratory, says: 'They are perfect!' Mina responds: 'We must always check.' What should we check upon receipt?
options: Color, shape, fit, and translucency
Only color
Only shape
Only price
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'All aesthetic criteria must be checked before placement.' Sami: 'I'll do a thorough check.'

questions.question: Mina, placing a veneer, says: 'We must use a light-cure adhesive system.' Sami asks: 'Why not self-cure?'
options: Light-cure offers better control of polymerization
Self-cure is faster
Light-cure is cheaper
Self-cure is more powerful
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Light-cure allows control of the polymerization timing.' Sami: 'I'll use light-cure for better control.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a veneer that is too white, says: 'The patient wanted it that way.' Mina responds: 'We must respect the limits.' Why avoid veneers that are too white?
options: A smile that is too white can look artificial and unaesthetic
White teeth are always more beautiful
White is the only acceptable color
Natural teeth are always very white
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The goal is a natural smile, not an artificial Hollywood smile.' Sami: 'I'll choose a more natural shade.'

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a smile, says: 'The golden ratio is respected.' Sami asks: 'What is the golden ratio?'
options: The 1:1.618 proportion between central and lateral incisors
The ideal color of teeth
The size of molars compared to premolars
The thickness of gums compared to teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The golden ratio is a mathematical proportion that creates natural harmony.' Sami: 'I'll always check this proportion.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a patient with worn teeth, says: 'Veneers will fix that.' Mina responds: 'Not without evaluating the cause.' Why evaluate the cause of wear?
options: Wear may be due to bruxism and require occlusal treatment
Wear is always age-related
Wear is always diet-related
Wear is always brushing-related
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Bruxism wear must be treated before placing veneers.' Sami: 'I'll do an occlusal analysis.'

questions.question: Mina, seeing a patient with tetracycline-stained teeth, says: 'Whitening won't be enough.' Sami asks: 'Why?'
options: Tetracyclines stain the dentin, not just the enamel
Whitening removes all stains
Tetracycline stains are superficial
Whitening is more effective on tetracycline stains
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Tetracyclines incorporate into the dentin, which whitening cannot reach.' Sami: 'I'll offer veneers rather than whitening.'

questions.question: Sami, preparing a veneer, says: 'I'll prepare with a bur.' Mina responds: 'Be careful with the enamel.' Why is preserving enamel crucial?
options: Enamel is the strongest layer and ensures adhesion
Enamel is not important for adhesion
Enamel regenerates easily
Enamel has no influence on color
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Enamel is essential for adhesion and resistance.' Sami: 'I'll preserve enamel as much as possible.'

questions.question: Mina, seeing a cracked veneer, says: 'It's a fatigue fracture.' Sami asks: 'What is that?'
options: A fracture due to repeated occlusal stresses
A fracture due to a single impact
A fracture due to a manufacturing defect
A fracture due to poor polishing
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Repeated occlusal stresses can cause progressive cracking.' Sami: 'I'll check the occlusion.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a patient with a gummy smile, says: 'We need longer veneers.' Mina responds: 'Not so fast!' What is the first approach?
options: Periodontal treatment to correct gingival excess
Immediate placement of elongated veneers
Gum whitening
Orthognathic surgery immediately
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Gingival excess is first treated with periodontal treatment.' Sami: 'I'll refer to a periodontist.'

questions.question: Mina, talking about composite veneers, says: 'They are cheaper but less durable.' Sami asks: 'When to use them?'
options: For temporary cases or limited budgets
Always, they are more aesthetic
Never, ceramic is always better
Only on molars
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Composite veneers are an economic alternative for simple cases.' Sami: 'I'll offer both options to the patient.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a poorly fitting veneer, says: 'It's acceptable.' Mina responds: 'Not at all!' Why is marginal fit crucial?
options: Poor fit can lead to caries or debonding
Fit is not important
Only the aesthetic aspect matters
Veneers are never perfectly fitted
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A defective marginal seal is an entry point for bacteria.' Sami: 'I'll check the fit meticulously.'

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a smile, says: 'The tooth axes are correct.' Sami asks: 'Why are axes important?'
options: Axes influence the perception of symmetry and harmony
Axes have no aesthetic importance
Axes only concern molars
Axes must be tilted to look natural
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A tilted axis can give the impression of an asymmetrical smile.' Sami: 'I'll always check the axes.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a patient with darkened teeth, says: 'Veneers will hide everything.' Mina responds: 'Not so sure.' When are veneers not indicated?
options: If the teeth are too devitalized and fragile
If the teeth are simply yellow
If the teeth are slightly stained
If the teeth have small cracks
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Devitalized teeth are fragile and may require crowns.' Sami: 'I'll evaluate the strength of the teeth.'

questions.question: Mina, seeing a patient with an asymmetrical smile, says: 'We need an orthodontic assessment.' Sami asks: 'Why?'
options: Orthodontics can correct asymmetries before aesthetics
Orthodontics is faster
Veneers correct asymmetries better
Orthodontics is cheaper
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Orthodontics treats the cause of the asymmetry.' Sami: 'I'll do an orthodontic assessment.'

questions.question: Sami, receiving veneers from the laboratory, says: 'They are perfect.' Mina responds: 'We must check the color under different lights.' Why?
options: Color can vary depending on lighting (natural, artificial)
Color is always the same
Light does not affect the color of veneers
The laboratory always knows the right color
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Veneers can have a different appearance in natural and artificial light.' Sami: 'I'll check under multiple lights.'

questions.question: Mina, seeing a patient with a gummy smile, says: 'It's a gummy smile.' Sami asks: 'How is it treated?'
options: By gingivectomy or aesthetic periodontal treatment
By placing elongated veneers
By gum whitening
By placing crowns on all teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Gingivectomy can correct excess gum.' Sami: 'I'll offer a gingivectomy.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a discolored veneer, says: 'It's the patient's fault.' Mina responds: 'Not necessarily.' What are the causes of veneer discoloration?
options: Wear, food stains, or inadequate polishing
Only tobacco and coffee
Only a poor shade choice
Only natural aging
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Veneers can discolor over time and with wear.' Sami: 'I'll inform the patient about necessary maintenance.'

questions.question: Mina, talking about veneers, says: 'Maintenance is essential.' Sami asks: 'What maintenance?'
options: Gentle brushing, regular scaling, and avoiding staining foods
Vigorous daily brushing
Monthly whitening
No particular maintenance
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Good maintenance extends the life of veneers.' Sami: 'I'll give maintenance advice to my patients.'

questions.question: Sami and Mina discuss the future of dental aesthetics. Sami says: 'AI will replace color choices!' Mina responds: 'Not so fast!' What is the future of aesthetics?
options: AI is a tool, but the human eye remains essential
AI will replace all aesthetic choices
Dental aesthetics will disappear
Patients will choose themselves with an app
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'AI can help, but the art of the smile is a matter of human sensitivity.' Sami: 'I agree, we keep our artist's eye!'
